# Venue: NeurIPS 2026 Main Track

Chosen on 2026-11-25 (venue-repo, answer to story-repo#2). Full requirement list with sources: `venue/neurips-2026-library.md` (the world's venue library, retrieved 2026-11-14). Template: `ht-role venue neurips --template DIR` (files `neurips_2026.sty`, `neurips_2026.tex`, `checklist.tex`).

## Why NeurIPS
- The objective asks for ICML, ICLR or NeurIPS, the latest official template, and "the venue's checklist (e.g. NeurIPS paper checklist)". NeurIPS is the only one of the three with a mandatory checklist that is part of the PDF, so the objective's checklist requirement has one unambiguous form.
- Single column, 5.5 in text block, 9 content pages: more room for figures and tables than ICML's 8 two-column pages. ICLR has the same 9 pages but no checklist and an edition already under review.
- Caveat on "latest": NeurIPS 2026 is the newest edition with a published call (the 2027 pages return 404 on 2026-11-14); its deadlines have passed, which does not matter for a template/standard. ICML 2027 / ICLR 2027 are newer editions; the objective allows any of the three, so this is a choice, not a gap. Re-check for NeurIPS 2027 only if the world's date passes its call.

## What binds the paper (all from the NeurIPS 2026 instructions and handbook)
- **Pages**: 9 content pages, figures and tables included. References, appendices, the checklist (and acknowledgments, which are hidden in anonymous mode) do not count and have no limit. Over-length is not reviewed. Camera-ready would be 10 pages (not needed here: a version is judged as a submission).
- **Layout**: US Letter, one column, text 5.5 in x 9 in, left margin 1.5 in; Times 10 pt on 11 pt; never edit the style file, margins or font sizes, never load `fullpage`/`geometry`/`savetrees`. Only Type 1 / embedded TrueType fonts (no Type 3 — matters for matplotlib: set `pdf.fonttype 42`).
- **Smallest type**: `\footnotesize` is 8 pt, `\scriptsize` 7 pt, `\tiny` 6 pt (style floors). The venue states no figure-font rule except "neat, clean and legible"; the paper's own standard is therefore: text inside figures at the size it prints, **not below 7 pt**, and preferably 8 pt or larger.
- **Float widths**: single-column page, so a full-width figure is `\linewidth` = 5.5 in; two side-by-side panels are about 2.7 in each; do not hand-position with absolute widths (give widths as multiples of `\linewidth`). Captions below figures, table title above tables, both lower-case except first word and proper nouns; the caption should state what is shown and a key take-away. Tables: `booktabs`, no vertical rules, centered. Figures should stay legible in black and white as well as colour.
- **Anonymous mode** (default, no `final`/`preprint`): no author names, no acknowledgments, own work in third person, links to code must be anonymous (an anonymised ZIP up to 100 MB is the safe form). The anonymous build prints line numbers and a "Submitted to NeurIPS 2026" footer; do not reference the line numbers.
- **Checklist**: mandatory, 16 items from `template/checklist.tex` (answers `\answerYes/\answerNo/\answerNA` plus a 1–2 sentence justification, questions unmodified, instruction block deleted but heading "NeurIPS Paper Checklist" kept). Placed after references and appendix; no page limit. A paper without it is desk-rejected. cd /hutian/repo/paper/sections; cat > setting.tex <<'EOF'
\section{Setting and estimands}
\label{sec:setting}

\paragraph{Search, report, verify.}
A benchmark pool of $N$ items and a declared space of $K$ configurations $\cfg$ (instruction wording, answer format, demonstrations) are given.
A search draws a set $S$ of $n$ items, evaluates $B\le K$ configurations on $S$, and returns the configuration $\chat$ with the highest score on $S$.
Writing $\hat A_S(\cfg)$ for the accuracy of $\cfg$ on $S$ and $\theta(\cfg)$ for its accuracy over the pool, the \emph{naive report} is $\hat A_S(\chat)$ and the \emph{gap} is $\hat A_S(\chat)-\theta(\chat)$.
Because $\chat$ is the maximiser of $B$ noisy scores, the gap has positive expectation even when no configuration is better than another; how large it is, and what drives it, is the question.

\paragraph{Fresh-item truth.}
The target of every number from the real LLM is the gap \emph{for this pool as the population}: $\theta(\chat)$ is measured on verification items disjoint from $S$ and from the demonstrations of $\chat$.
The statement is not about MMLU-Pro at large, about other models, or about configuration spaces other than the one searched.
Because verification items are finite, the measured fresh accuracy carries sampling noise of its own; it has zero mean and enters every reported gap as a stated noise floor.

\paragraph{Three estimands.}
Reporting protocols claim different things, and are scored on their own claim.
(i)~The accuracy $\theta(\chat)$ of the configuration actually deployed: claimed by the naive report, by lower bounds, and by a held-out split report (whose $\chat$ is chosen on fewer items and is a different configuration).
(ii)~The expected accuracy $\EE\,\theta(\chat)$ of the search procedure: claimed by nested cross-validation and optimism bootstrap.
(iii)~A common yardstick at equal total item budget $N_{\mathrm{tot}}$: how often a point report overstates $\theta(\chat)$, the coverage and tightness of one-sided lower bounds at equal nominal level, and the true accuracy lost by spending items on reporting instead of search.

\paragraph{Effective number of configurations.}
Configurations that differ in wording are far from independent, so the nominal $K$ overstates how many competitors the maximum is taken over.
We define $\Keff$ operationally as the number of independent configurations whose expected maximum of standardised Gaussian scores equals that of the observed, correlated configurations (computed from the item-level covariance of the search log), and write $\sigmatheta$ for the standard deviation of the true accuracies $\theta(\cfg)$ across configurations.
EOF

shown.message:
The paper skeleton is on `paper-repo`'s `dev` and builds in the NeurIPS 2026 template. The abstract, introduction and appendix are empty until results exist. Written so far:
- **Related work:** four groups, with citations from `idea-repo`'s `prior_work.md`.
- **Setting and estimands:** the search → report → verify protocol, the fresh-item target, the three estimands and the effective number of configurations.
- **Bibliography:** 28 entries, written from `prior_work.md`. They are not yet checked against sources, so this needs doing before any version goes out.

Paths are declared in `.forgejo/document.json` and `.forgejo/CODEOWNERS`: sources in `paper/`, the PDF built to `paper/main.pdf`, and the checklist in `paper/checklist.tex` (not yet filled in). I answered and closed `venue-repo`'s request in `paper-repo`#4 with these paths.

The method and experiment sections wait on `experiment-repo`'s results and its confirmation of how each result is computed. The checklist waits on facts from `experiment-repo` (compute used, seeds, licences). I haven't offered a version yet.
